claim: Emergent traffic network optimization through reinforcement learning at each intersection
mechanism: Each intersection operates as an independent reinforcement learning agent that maximizes a local reward function (e.g., vehicles served per cycle) while receiving limited state information from neighbors, with the collective behavior emerging as optimal network performance
evidence: Myxomycetes optimize network structures through local feedback
Reinforcement learning has shown success in traffic signal control
Distributed multi-agent systems can solve complex optimization problems
assumptions: Local reward maximization leads to global optimum
Limited neighbor communication provides sufficient state information for decision-making
Reinforcement learning can converge within the required time frame
Traffic patterns exhibit sufficient regularity for learning
expected_failure_modes: Suboptimal policies due to limited reward design
Catastrophic forgetting when traffic patterns change
novelty_rationale: Applies the principle of local adaptation with emergent global optimization through learning mechanisms rather than predetermined control rules, allowing the system to discover optimal timing patterns through experience
testability: Can be tested by implementing RL agents at each intersection with varying learning rates and reward functions, measuring performance across different traffic scenarios
falsifier: If the system fails to learn an optimal policy within reasonable time (e.g., 2 weeks of simulated operation) or if performance degrades compared to a simple proportional control system
